item.title: Coalition Intelligence Sharing and the Limits of Trust
item.dc:creator: Maria Lopez
Tom Reed
item.description:
Volume 41, Issue 6, December 2026, Page 812-835.
Abstract. Intelligence sharing within coalitions is widely assumed to deepen with alliance duration. Drawing on declassified records from three multinational operations between 1991 and 2011, this article argues that sharing is limited less by distrust of partners than by domestic legal restrictions and classification systems. It finds that informal liaison networks repeatedly compensated for formal barriers, and it proposes a typology of four sharing arrangements.

item.title: Strategic Warning in the Age of Commercial Satellites
item.dc:creator: Lee Chen
item.description: Commercial satellite imagery has transformed strategic warning. Using case studies of troop build-ups observed by private firms before 2022, the article shows how open imagery shortened decision timelines for governments and created new pressures on intelligence agencies to declassify their own assessments quickly. It concludes that warning has become a public process.
